title: My thoughts on Meshy vs. Tripo3D
author: Aineisa
selftext:
As a long time user of Meshy and now Tripo I thought my experiences might be helpful for those who havent tried them yet. 

Short version: Tripo3D wins but still has room for improvement. 

Long version: 

Meshy pros.   
\- AI agent. Tell it what I want, give references, and it handles getting what I want. Also makes it easy to organize projects since all the references and generations sit in the same screen space. Still it tends to give up too easily and is annoyingly verbose.   
\- slightly larger animation library but I don’t use them. 

Tripo3D.  
\- segmentation. I no longer have to manually edit to get the tank turrets separated from the hulls  
\- retopology  
\- reducing polycounts. Decimating in blender can only bring me so far. Tripo does really well at reducing polycounts.   
\- midjourney available. Midjourney has always been very creative in what it generates so having access to it in Tripo is an unexpected plus.  

It really feels like Meshy has fallen far behind. 

I’ll be sticking with Tripo for 3D but using the remainder of my Meshy subscription for 2D work since it is very helpful keeping things organized in the agent project.

ay around?

replies.author: Aineisa
replies.body: Tripo3D subscription let’s you also use midjourney

comments.author: futuneral
comments.body:
This comparison is a bit confusing. Meshy has retopo and poly count reduction, instead of Midjourney it uses what looks like nano banana (just judging by the output). So feature by feature they are on par, maybe you could talk about the quality differencea there? Segmentation would be a killer feature for Meshy, but I won't be able to give up their agent. The best feature of it is that it keeps the context, all concept art and then assets came out in the same style and it also serves as a project folder.
You also didn't talk about actual 3D generation. Any advantages to either of them?

replies.author: Aineisa
replies.body:
3D generation is really going to depend on what youre generating. 

I find Tripo has better reduction and retopology. Meshys reduction, for me at least, creates a lot of distortions. 

Meshy has banana and a few others but having access to midjourney in the same subscription is a big win. I’ve used midjourney since it started and it’s always been creative with the prompts which is helpful if I’m fishing for something unique. 

Should you switch to Tripo if you’re happy with Meshy? I’d say it’s worth it if you want segmentation. 

In the past when creating 3D posed printable models in Meshy I would have to redo the weight painting and modelling to separate clothing pieces before rigging. With segmentation I just group the pieces I want together and then let it do the rigging. Way easier.
